title: Hierarchical cross-window mixing for PNN-v1
research_question: Can a second low-fan-in Q.ANT Fourier/KAN stage improve ECG200 validation accuracy by learning interactions between neighboring temporal windows?
hypothesis: Alpha1 loses useful temporal information because its 12 local 8->4 blocks remain independent until the final global classifier. A second Q.ANT-native low-fan-in mixing stage over neighboring window representations can improve task performance while retaining a hierarchical photonic-native structure.
frozen_candidates: alpha1 control: 12 local 8->4 blocks, concatenate 48, Fourier/KAN 48->2 head
alpha2 hierarchical mixer: 12 local 8->4 blocks; pair adjacent 4+4 features into 6 Fourier/KAN 8->4 mixer blocks; concatenate 24; Fourier/KAN 24->2 head

data_protocol.selection_rule: Reuse the exact deterministic stratified TRAIN/validation boundary from Exp003. Compare only the two frozen candidates across the same fixed seeds. Freeze the selected architecture before canonical TEST evaluation.
data_protocol.test_boundary: Canonical TEST must not influence architecture selection.

design_constraints: Keep the first-stage 12 local 8->4 Fourier/KAN blocks unchanged.
Change exactly one architectural concept: add a neighboring-window Q.ANT-native mixing stage.
Report reference and Q.ANT evaluation separately.
primary_metric: Validation mean Q.ANT accuracy across the 10 fixed seeds, with standard deviation reported alongside it.
secondary_metrics: canonical TEST accuracy after selection is frozen
success_criteria: Alpha2 hierarchical mixer must have higher mean validation Q.ANT accuracy than alpha1 and validation Q.ANT accuracy standard deviation no more than 0.01 absolute above alpha1.
hardware_boundary: Software/simulation-backend experiment only; no real photonic hardware performance claim.
next_gate: Implement and review PNN-v1 Exp004, then add it to the guarded approval allowlist.
